jobs.description: Employer: Steel Dynamics, Inc. - Aluminum Dynamics Expires: 10/10/2026 What Does Steel Dynamics Do?Steel Dynamics is a leading industrial metals solutions company that produces lower-carbon, high-quality steel products primarily from recycled scrap. Operating through a circular manufacturing model, the company manufactures a wide range of steel products including flat roll, structural, and long products for industries such as construction, automotive, energy, and manufacturing. In addition to steel production, Steel Dynamics operates metals recycling facilities, steel fabrication plants, and aluminum production operations, serving customers across North America with a focus on innovation, efficiency, and sustainability.What Makes This Internship Different?Steel Dynamics’ electrical engineering internships stand out from those at other companies because they offer a true balance of office-based engineering work and hands-on industrial experience. Interns are not limited to observing from a distance, they actively work alongside operators and maintenance teams on the production floor, applying engineering principles directly to equipment, systems, and processes. This approach allows interns to design solutions, test them in real-world conditions, and see the immediate impact of their work. Internship LocationThis internship is located at the Steel Dynamics Columbus Flat Roll Division located in Columbus, MS. This internship will take place part-time throughout the 2026-2027 school year, with potential to work full-time hours in Summer 2027. Interested students must be located in the Great Columbus, MS area, ideally enrolled at Mississippi State University. Internship BenefitsFurnished Housing Free of CostProvided for interns living more than 50 miles from their work site, including essential furnishings to ensure a comfortable stay during the internship.401(k) & Company MatchEligibility to participate in the company 401(k) plan with a 10–50% company match that vests immediately.Employee DiscountsAccess to discounts on hotels, vehicles, and other goods and services through Steel Dynamics’ nationwide partner network.Employee Assistance ProgramUp to five free visits per issue, per year for counseling, legal advice, financial guidance, and other daily living resources.Intern ExtravaganzaA two-day event at company headquarters featuring facility tours, networking with company leaders, cultural immersion, and connecting with other interns from across the country.Competitive PayCompetitive hourly wages for all internship positions, rewarding the value interns bring to the company. What Are My Responsibilities as an Automation/Controls Engineering Intern at Steel Dynamics?Follow all safety policies, participate in risk assessments, and support lockout/tagout (LOTO) verification under supervision.Assist with PLC and HMI programming, testing, troubleshooting, and documentation for industrial automation systems.Support automation projects through programming, software development, and control system modifications under the guidance of engineering mentors.Develop and maintain control system documentation, including electrical schematics, network diagrams, operating procedures, and technical reports.Assist with automation hardware selection, specification, and implementation for equipment upgrades and new projects.Support troubleshooting efforts involving PLCs, HMIs, industrial networks, instrumentation, drives, and control system hardware.Work with Siemens automation platforms, including STEP 7 and TIA Portal.Support HMI and visualization updates and develop dashboards or reports.Assist with industrial networking activities and device communications troubleshooting.Participate in planned outages, equipment upgrades, start-ups, and commissioning activities by executing test plans and verifying system functionality.Create and maintain software, database, and configuration backups while following change management procedures.Collaborate with operators, electricians, mechanics, maintenance personnel, IT, and production teams to implement automation improvements.Document troubleshooting activities, standard work procedures, and project outcomes to support knowledge transfer and long-term system reliability. What Qualifications Do I Need?RequiredCurrently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Automation/Controls Engineering, or a related field.Basic understanding of programming principles and troubleshooting methodologies.Strong interest in industrial automation, controls engineering, and manufacturing technology.Ability to work effectively in a team-oriented industrial environment.PreferredExposure to programming through coursework, projects, or personal experience.Exposure to electrical, computer, embedded, or control system concepts through coursework or projects.Interest in hands-on troubleshooting and applying engineering concepts in an industrial environment.Previous technical project, laboratory, internship, co-op, or other hands-on experience.Steel Dynamics, Inc., and all affiliated entities are equal opportunity employers.

jobs.title: Structural Engineering Intern at Steel Dynamics, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Steel Dynamics, Inc. - New Millennium Building Systems Expires: 10/10/2026 What Does Steel Dynamics Do?Steel Dynamics is a leading industrial metals solutions company that produces lower-carbon, high-quality steel products primarily from recycled scrap. Operating through a circular manufacturing model, the company manufactures a wide range of steel products including flat roll, structural, and long products for industries such as construction, automotive, energy, and manufacturing. In addition to steel production, Steel Dynamics operates metals recycling facilities, steel fabrication plants, and aluminum production operations, serving customers across North America with a focus on innovation, efficiency, and sustainability. This is a New Millennium Position. Who is New Millennium?A division of Steel Dynamics Inc. (SDI), New Millennium was founded in 1999 in Butler, Indiana, with one clear mission: To be a trusted collaborator for the design, engineering, and supply of structural steel joists and deck. Today, 25 years later, we’re one of the largest providers of high-performance structural steel joists, joist girders, and deck solutions for commercial steel construction projects. What Makes This Internship Different?The Structural Engineering Internship at Steel Dynamics is unique because interns are not limited to observing or performing routine tasks, they are directly involved in projects that impact production, safety, and long-term infrastructure reliability. Unlike many programs that focus solely on classroom-style assignments, SDI interns gain hands-on experience in both design and field work, from analyzing and drafting structural components to inspecting and reinforcing critical infrastructure in active industrial environments. This combination of office and on-site project involvement provides students with exposure to the full lifecycle of civil engineering work in a manufacturing setting. Many interns also work alongside contractors, operators, and engineers, giving them a broader perspective of how civil engineering integrates with operations and business strategy. The result is an experience that goes beyond traditional internships by preparing students to solve real-world challenges and contribute measurable value from day one. Internship LocationThis internship is located at the New Millennium facility located in Hope, AR, in the Sales Department. This internship will take place during Summer 2027. Internship BenefitsFurnished Housing Free of CostProvided for interns living more than 50 miles from their work site, including essential furnishings to ensure a comfortable stay during the internship.401(k) & Company MatchEligibility to participate in the company 401(k) plan with a 10–50% company match that vests immediately.Employee DiscountsAccess to discounts on hotels, vehicles, and other goods and services through Steel Dynamics’ nationwide partnernetwork.Employee Assistance ProgramUp to five free visits per issue, per year for counseling, legal advice, financial guidance, and other daily living resources.Intern ExtravaganzaA two-day event at company headquarters featuring facility tours, networking with company leaders, cultural immersion, and connecting with other interns from across the country.Competitive PayCompetitive hourly wages for all internship positions, rewarding the value interns bring to the company. What Are My Responsibilities as a Structural Engineering Intern at Steel Dynamics?Apply engineering principles to support ongoing design, analysis, and construction projects ranging from community churches, schools, offices and retail buildings to athletic facilities and fieldhouses to massive warehouses and data centers covering acres of land for the world’s largest distribution and data storage companies.Assist in evaluating and designing structural components such as platforms, open-web steel joists and girders, and welded and bolted connections.Conduct inspections of existing infrastructure to identify potential issues and recommend solutions.Perform experiments, collect field data, and analyze results to guide project decisions and operational improvements.Utilize laboratory and engineering tools, including AutoCAD and BIM software, to create drawings, models, and technical documentation.Collaborate with engineers, contractors, and operations personnel to clarify requirements, coordinate repairs, and support project execution.Ensure compliance with applicable building codes, safety standards, and internal quality expectations.Contribute to day-to-day engineering activities in a fast-paced industrial environment to meet facility needs.Assist sales team with technical knowledge to complete estimates, troubleshoot scope issues with estimating and coordinators to help find issues at bid time.Value engineer to help with design options and partner with key customers to offer competitive options. What Qualifications Do I Need?Candidates should have a strong interest in Structural Engineering, and be enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program in Civil Engineering or related field, enabling attainment of EIT license and eventual Civil PE licensure.Preferred GPA of at least 2.7Examples of Projects Steel Dynamics Structural Engineering Interns Have CompletedDesign and analyze structures such as buildings, crane runways, mezzanines, platforms, and equipment supports to ensure long-term durability under industrial conditions.Evaluate structural loading, vibration, thermal expansion, and wear to ensure all designs can withstand heavy and dynamic forces over time.Ensure all designs comply with local building codes, OSHA safety regulations, and industry-specific standards through thorough documentation and review.Participate in structural detailing using AutoCAD, converting structural drawings into fabrication-ready drawings and details.Generate finalized modification details to resolve field conflicts and coordinate with information provided by outside parties to ensure project success.Steel Dynamics, Inc., and all affiliated entities are equal opportunity employers.

jobs.title: Structural Engineering Intern at Degenkolb Engineers
jobs.description: Employer: Degenkolb Engineers Expires: 10/10/2026 Who We AreFounded in 1940 and headquartered in San Francisco, Degenkolb Engineers helps make complex, high-stakes projects real. We bring deep technical expertise, disciplined creativity, and a practical understanding of construction to every challenge; building strong relationships early, making complexity easier to navigate, and keeping the success of projects central to our work.Our teams deliver customized structural solutions across healthcare, education, science and technology, forensics, construction engineering, federal buildings, and other complex markets. Whether a project calls for navigating stringent codes, balancing budget and schedule, solving an unusual technical problem, or creating a landmark structural system, we connect the right people and ideas to develop solutions that serve our clients and communities.The Internship OpportunityDegenkolb is again offering a summer internship program for future structural engineers. The program is designed to complement your academic training with an inside look at how a structural engineering practice operates and to give you meaningful, hands-on experience with active project work. Many former interns return to Degenkolb as full-time employees after completing their studies.Turn classroom knowledge into meaningful project experience with trusted mentors and a team invested in your future.Internships with flexible summer start dates are available in Los Angeles, Oakland, Orange County, Sacramento, San Diego, San Francisco, California, Seattle, Washington, and Detroit and Grand Rapids, Michigan. You may indicate interest in multiple locations on a single application; candidates are considered for one location at a time based on ranked preferences and office availability.Who Thrives Here You are an upper-level civil or structural engineering student whose education will continue through at least the Fall 2027 semester. You are curious, collaborative, and eager to connect classroom concepts with real-world structural engineering. You may be especially interested in seismic analysis for our West Coast offices or steel design for our Michigan offices. You want an internship where you can ask thoughtful questions, contribute to meaningful work, learn from experienced engineers, and better understand how technical decisions serve clients and communities. You are ready to take ownership of your learning while being supported by a culture of excellence.What You'll ExperienceAcademic coursework provides the foundation. Hands-on experience is where engineering comes to life. As a Structural Engineering Intern, you will work alongside experienced engineers on active projects, applying classroom concepts while developing practical skills and professional confidence.Meaningful Project Work: Contribute to active structural engineering projects and see how project teams turn technical knowledge into practical solutions for clients.Technical Learning: Build skills in structural analysis and design, project delivery, and site observation while gaining exposure to real-world engineering challenges.Mentorship & Feedback: Learn directly from experienced engineers who will provide context, answer questions, share candid feedback, and help you understand the purpose behind the work.Firmwide Perspectives: Participate in a summer presentation series featuring engineers and firm leaders from across Degenkolb. Past topics have included sustainability, LEANSTEEL®, construction administration, earthquake reconnaissance, practice-area overviews, leadership conversations, and career development.Connection & Collaboration: Work with multidisciplinary project teams and build meaningful relationships with professionals across offices and practice areas.Career Exploration: Expand your professional network, strengthen your engineering judgment, and gain insight into career paths within structural engineering and at Degenkolb.Minimum RequirementsAcademic Status: Must be a continuing student enrolled through at least the Fall 2027 semester. This includes: A current full-time Civil Engineering Senior (Juniors who meet the other requirements may be considered) planning to transition directly into a Structural Engineering graduate program in Fall 2027.A current, first-year Graduate student in multi-year Structural Engineering master’s or Ph.D. program.Required Coursework: The following courses must be completed by the internship start date.Structural AnalysisSteel DesignReinforced Concrete DesignAcademic Performance: Strong performance in upper-division civil or structural engineering coursework, with a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.40. Strong academic performance in graduate coursework is expected, where applicable.Technical Focus: Demonstrated passion for structural engineering, with a preferred interest in seismic analysis for West Coast offices or steel design for Michigan offices.Leadership & Involvement: Leadership roles or active participation in extracurricular activities, engineering societies such as ASCE or SEI, or other pursuits.Work Authorization: Current authorization to work in the United States for any employer.Compensation The hourly pay range for this position across our offices is $30.50 to $39.50 per hour. This range is a good-faith estimate provided pursuant to applicable pay transparency laws. Actual pay will be based on factors including work location, company geographic differentials, education level, and candidate qualifications.Scholarship Program Interns hired into the program are eligible to apply for Degenkolb's competitive scholarships:One scholarship for Cal Poly San Luis Obispo studentsOne scholarship for students at other California State University campusesOne scholarship for University of California students, with preference given to members of AISES, NSBE, SHPE, or WISEEach award is a $4,000 grant, payable after registration for the Fall 2027 quarter or semester.Scholarship Application Requirements Applications are due March 1, 2027. Submit a scholarship statement of no more than two pages addressing:Career goals in the structural engineering professionGraduate school education goalsAcademic and leadership accomplishmentsChallenges overcome in your academic journey, such as the experience of being a first-generation college studentQuestions? Contact Michelle Chapman at mchapman@degenkolb.com.Degenkolb also participates in the NCSEA Diversity in Structural Engineering Scholarship Program.Our CultureDegenkolb is a place where technical rigor and human connection strengthen one another. Our flexible work environment brings together experts who are generous with their knowledge, proud of employee ownership, engaged in the profession, and respectful of life outside of work.As an intern, you will experience focused professional development within a supportive and transparent team. You will be encouraged to contribute your perspective, learn through purposeful challenges, and build relationships that can continue well beyond the summer. Learn more about life at Degenkolb.How to ApplyApply externally at https://degenkolb.com/job-openings/ Please include:ResumeUnofficial undergraduate and graduate transcripts, as applicable - required for considerationA targeted cover letter describing why you want to work at Degenkolb and how your background, interests, and goals align with this opportunity - strongly encouraged​​YOUR CURIOSITY. REAL PROJECTS. MEANINGFUL IMPACT.Bring what you're learning. We'll help you see where it can take you.

jobs.title: Material Engineering Co-op III (Spring/Summer 2027 or Summer/Fall 2027) at BAE Systems, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: BAE Systems, Inc. Expires: 10/10/2026 Job Description You don’t see it, but it’s there. Our employees work on the world’s most advanced electronics – from saving emissions in the City of Lights to powering the Mars Rover to protecting the F35 fighter jet. At Electronic Systems, you’ll be among the brightest minds, working on the aerospace and defense industry’s most difficult problems. Drawing strength from our differences, we’re innovating for the future. And you can, too. Our flexible work environment provides you a chance to change the world without giving up your personal life. We put our customers first – exemplified by our missions: “We Protect Those Who Protect Us®” and “We Innovate For Those Who Move The WorldTM.” Sound like a team you want to be a part of? Come build your career with BAE Systems.BAE Systems is looking for a Material Engineer with a passion for engineering and the desire to be part of an innovative, dedicated team responsible for industry-leading Global Positioning Systems (GPS) products. Our team needs someone interested in hands-on experience working in a Material and Component Evaluation lab. This position offers abundant opportunity to acquire in-depth knowledge of materials used in electronic assemblies, techniques used for failure analysis and work in a team environment.Assignments may include tasks such as obtaining dimensional measurements of parts, XRF analysis, FTIR Analysis, cross-sectioning, testing material properties, failure analysis of electronic parts or assemblies and evaluating new processes. The successful applicant should be knowledgeable of lab practices and basic lab equipment.Because of the need for consistent, in-person collaboration and/or the requirement to perform all work onsite due to the nature of this particular role, it will be performed full-time on site. This means work will be conducted on location at a BAE Systems facility 100% of the time.In this position, you will participate in BAE Systems' nationwide LEAP Internship & Co-op Program, where you will Learn, Engage, Apply, and Progress within the company. The LEAP Program will provide you with the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals on impactful projects, engage in career development opportunities, and network with our business leaders and the other students in the program.Required Education, Experience, & Skills Applicant must be pursuing a STEM degree in an applicable engineering or science field of Material Engineering, Chemical Engineering or ChemistrySophomore or Junior year of collegeExperience with lab equipmentPreferred Education, Experience, & Skills Prefer applicants pursuing a Material Engineering degreeExperience with cross-sectioningAbility to work with a diverse teamA genuine desire to learn and innovateEnjoys failure analysisPay InformationFull-Time Salary Range: $42931 - $57949Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.Temporary employees generally are not eligible for BAE Systems benefits, but can elect to participate in the 401(k) savings plan. Temporary employees working 20+ hours per week are eligible for medical benefits, the employee assistance program, and business travel accident insurance.About BAE Systems Electronic SystemsBAE Systems, Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of BAE Systems plc, an international defense, aerospace and security company which delivers a full range of products and services for air, land and naval forces, as well as advanced electronics, security, information technology solutions and customer support services. Improving the future and protecting lives is an ambitious mission, but it’s what we do at BAE Systems. Working here means using your passion and ingenuity where it counts – defending national security with breakthrough technology, superior products, and intelligence solutions. As you develop the latest technology and defend national security, you will continually hone your skills on a team—making a big impact on a global scale. At BAE Systems, you’ll find a rewarding career that truly makes a difference. Electronic Systems (ES) is the global innovator behind BAE Systems’ game-changing defense and commercial electronics. Exploiting every electron, we push the limits of what is possible, giving our customers the edge and our employees opportunities to change the world. Our products and capabilities can be found everywhere – from the depths of the ocean to the far reaches of space. At our core are more than 14,000 highly talented Electronic Systems employees with the brightest minds in the industry, we make an impact – for our customers and the communities we serve.

jobs.feedName: Andrew J. Anagnost College of Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.title: Electrical Engineering Intern at Steel Dynamics, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Steel Dynamics, Inc. - New Millennium Building Systems Expires: 10/10/2026 What Does Steel Dynamics Do?Steel Dynamics is a leading industrial metals solutions company that produces lower-carbon, high-quality steel products primarily from recycled scrap. Operating through a circular manufacturing model, the company manufactures a wide range of steel products including flat roll, structural, and long products for industries such as construction, automotive, energy, and manufacturing. In addition to steel production, Steel Dynamics operates metals recycling facilities, steel fabrication plants, and aluminum production operations, serving customers across North America with a focus on innovation, efficiency, and sustainability.What Makes This Internship Different?Steel Dynamics’ electrical engineering internships stand out from those at other companies because they offer a true balance of office-based engineering work and hands-on industrial experience. Interns are not limited to observing from a distance, they actively work alongside operators and maintenance teams on the production floor, applying engineering principles directly to equipment, systems, and processes. This approach allows interns to design solutions, test them in real-world conditions, and see the immediate impact of their work. Internship LocationThis internship is located at the Steel Dynamics Roanoke Bar Division located in Roanoke, VA, in the Engineering Department. This internship will take place during the Summer 2027 term. Internship BenefitsFurnished Housing Free of CostProvided for interns living more than 50 miles from their work site, including essential furnishings to ensure a comfortable stay during the internship.401(k) & Company MatchEligibility to participate in the company 401(k) plan with a 10–50% company match that vests immediately.Employee DiscountsAccess to discounts on hotels, vehicles, and other goods and services through Steel Dynamics’ nationwide partner network.Employee Assistance ProgramUp to five free visits per issue, per year for counseling, legal advice, financial guidance, and other daily living resources.Intern ExtravaganzaA two-day event at company headquarters featuring facility tours, networking with company leaders, cultural immersion, and connecting with other interns from across the country.Competitive PayCompetitive hourly wages for all internship positions, rewarding the value interns bring to the company. What Are My Responsibilities as an Electrical Engineering Intern at Steel Dynamics?Assist with substation reliability and preventative maintenance through inspections, documentation, and spare parts planning.Support engineering teams on safety initiatives, including labeling, schematic review, and lockout/tagout procedures.Participate in upgrade and installation projects by reviewing diagrams, updating schematics, and supporting system documentation.Contribute to instrumentation and control projects by assisting with HMI programming, logic development, and monitoring systems.Assist in troubleshooting and repairing electrical systems, including sourcing replacement components and supporting system restoration.Perform inventory management tasks such as cataloging materials, preparing bills of materials, and assisting with procurement planning.Gain hands-on field experience by shadowing electricians during installations, maintenance, and troubleshooting.Collaborate with contractors, vendors, and internal teams on electrical projects and process improvements. What Qualifications Do I Need?Candidates should be enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program in Electrical Engineering or Electrical Engineering Technology.Degree program or experience should include one or more of the following: electrical machinery, power distribution, PLCs/automation systems, power electronics/drives.Preferred GPA of at least 2.7.Examples of Projects Steel Dynamics Electrical Engineering Interns Have CompletedSupport substation reliability by inspecting and documenting current conditions of PTs (Potential Transformers) and CTs (Current Transformers), preparing inventories of available spares, and identifying components that require ordering for contingency planning.Assist with preventative maintenance of high-voltage substations, including reading equipment nameplates, assessing transformer health, and developing documentation based on OEM specifications and site safety standards.Collaborate with engineering teams to optimize safety practices by applying arc flash labels, observing lockout/tagout procedures, and reinforcing “trust but verify” principles when interpreting electrical schematics and prints.Participate in substation upgrade projects by tracing wire diagrams, creating custom wire labels, updating schematics, and loosely managing documentation for labeling systems across GE and TMEIC controls.Contribute to instrumentation and control design by programming HMIs such as C-more for real-time temperature displays and developing logic in Studio 5000 to automate screen changes for furnace monitoring systems.Assist in troubleshooting and rebuilding damaged electrical systems, including camera systems like UNILUX used for surface inspection, and sourcing replacement components for system restoration.Verify and correct electrical blueprints for major furnace systems (e.g., Round-Top-Melter, Tilter-Holder-Furnace), documenting any discrepancies and updating plans to improve installation accuracy and efficiency.Perform electrical inventory management by cataloging leftover materials from previous installations, preparing bill of materials for upcoming commissioning projects, and supporting procurement planning.Gain hands-on experience with field installations and maintenance tasks by shadowing electricians during troubleshooting, learning conduit work, motor disassembly, wiring practices, and electrical safety standards in live industrial environments.Support cross-functional communication by coordinating with contractors, vendors, and internal departments on projects involving trailer power feeds, radiation detector values, and cold mill upgrades, while learning foundational concepts in power distribution and teamwork.Steel Dynamics, Inc., and all affiliated entities are equal opportunity employers.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 - Software Engineering Internship at Western Digital
jobs.description: Employer: Western Digital Expires: 10/10/2026 This posting supports current and anticipated early-career hiring needs. Applying allows our recruiting team to consider you for opportunities that align with your qualifications, preferences, and availability. An immediate opening or interview is not guaranteed.Where are these roles located? You’ll have the opportunity to work with teams in:Colorado Springs, ColoradoIrvine, CaliforniaLongmont, ColoradoFremont, CaliforniaRochester, MinnesotaSan Jose, CaliforniaSystem Tools Software Intern:Build the software behind the technology.As a System Tools Software Intern, you'll create the software that powers engineering teams and next-generation products. You'll design, develop, test, and improve tools that make systems faster, more reliable, and easier to build.In this role, you may:Design and develop system software, utilities, and engineering tools.Build or enhance operating systems, compilers, networking tools, databases, and Internet-based applications.Troubleshoot, debug, and optimize software performance.Collaborate with hardware and software engineers to ensure seamless integration.Help influence hardware design by developing software that works efficiently with new technologies.Applications Software Intern:Create software that helps teams work smarter.As an Applications Software Engineer, you'll develop applications that support employees, customers, and business operations. You'll design, build, test, and improve software used across enterprise systems.In this role, you may:Design, develop, and maintain commercial and internal software applications.Write clean, efficient, and maintainable code using modern programming languages.Test, debug, and improve application performance.Collaborate with teammates to build new features and solve technical problems.Create documentation that supports software deployment and ongoing maintenance.Data Analytics Intern:Turn data into insights that drive better decisions.As a Data Analytics Engineer, you'll build the tools and data systems that help teams understand performance, improve products, and solve business challenges. You'll work with large datasets to create meaningful insights that influence engineering and business decisions.In this role, you may:Design and develop data pipelines, databases, and data warehouses.Build software and automation tools for collecting, processing, and analyzing data.Create dashboards, reports, and visualizations that support decision-making.Partner with stakeholders to understand business needs and translate them into technical solutions.Analyze data to identify trends, improve processes, and solve complex problems.Firmware Engineering Intern:Write the code that brings hardware to life.As a Firmware Intern, you'll develop the low-level software that allows hardware devices to function. Working at the intersection of hardware and software, you'll help build reliable, high-performance embedded systems used in next-generation technology.In this role, you may:Design, develop, test, and debug embedded firmware.Write software using C, C++, assembly, and other low-level programming languages.Collaborate with hardware engineers to integrate software with electronic systems.Troubleshoot firmware and hardware interactions to improve performance and reliability.Support new product development from concept through production.This role is part of WD's early career development program. WD's early career development program is ideal for individuals at the early stages of their professional career. Participants receive foundational training through structured onboarding, mentorship, and a curated development curriculum. The responsibilities of this role are typically aligned with candidates who have approximately 0–2+ years of relevant professional experience, though candidates of all experience levels are encouraged to apply.Systems Design & Integration Intern:Bring complex systems together.As a Systems Design & Integration Engineer, you'll help ensure hardware and software work together seamlessly. You'll collaborate across engineering teams to design, integrate, test, and optimize complete system solutions for next-generation products.In this role, you may:Define system requirements and technical specifications.Evaluate hardware and software compatibility.Coordinate the integration of multiple subsystems into complete products.Identify, troubleshoot, and resolve system-level issues.Recommend improvements that enhance system performance, reliability, and scalability. Qualifications Required:Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.Experience developing technical skills through coursework, internships, research, or personal projects using one or more programming languages such as C, C++, Python, Java, Go (Golang), SQL, JavaScript, or similar technologies.Familiarity with software development fundamentals, debugging, data structures, algorithms, operating systems, or other computer engineering concepts.Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills with a passion for learning new technologies.Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment.Proficiency with Microsoft Office and common software development tools (such as Git, Linux, or IDEs) is a plus.Interest in storage technologies, semiconductors, embedded systems, cloud computing, AI, data analytics, or other emerging technologies.

jobs.title: Structural Analysis Engineer Intern at Bechtel Plant Machinery, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Bechtel Plant Machinery, Inc. Expires: 10/10/2026 Job Title: Structural Analysis Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)Location: Schenectady, New YorkStatus: InternHourly Rate: $28 Job SummaryAs a Structural Analysis Engineer Intern at BPMI, you will perform routine technical functions to execute the BPMI mission in areas including, but not limited to performing a wide range of engineering tasks related to the analysis, design, and evaluation of structural components and systems, ensuring compliance with NR program and safety standards. This role involves utilizing engineering tools and methods to assess structural integrity and generate technical reports. The engineer works closely with various teams to integrate engineering solutions into broader program goals, while providing technical support for field operations.This opportunity will begin Summer 2027, working a full-time schedule (40 hours/week). Please note, this is not a remote position. You will be expected to come into the office for this opportunity.Our internship will give you the opportunity to work in your field of study while simultaneously pursuing your bachelor’s degree at an accredited college or university. These opportunities can enhance your academic training while teaching critical business skills and allowing you to learn about BPMI, the Navy, and the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program. jobs.description: Employer: Steel Dynamics, Inc. - Steel Dynamics, Inc. Expires: 10/10/2026 What Does Steel Dynamics Do?Steel Dynamics is a leading industrial metals solutions company that produces lower-carbon, high-quality steel products primarily from recycled scrap. Operating through a circular manufacturing model, the company manufactures a wide range of steel products including flat roll, structural, and long products for industries such as construction, automotive, energy, and manufacturing. In addition to steel production, Steel Dynamics operates metals recycling facilities, steel fabrication plants, and aluminum production operations, serving customers across North America with a focus on innovation, efficiency, and sustainability.What Makes This Internship Different?Steel Dynamics’ electrical engineering internships stand out from those at other companies because they offer a true balance of office-based engineering work and hands-on industrial experience. Interns are not limited to observing from a distance, they actively work alongside operators and maintenance teams on the production floor, applying engineering principles directly to equipment, systems, and processes. This approach allows interns to design solutions, test them in real-world conditions, and see the immediate impact of their work. Internship LocationThis internship is located at the Steel Dynamics Flat Roll Division located in Sinton, TX, in the Casting Department. This internship will take place in Summer 2027. Internship BenefitsFurnished Housing Free of CostProvided for interns living more than 50 miles from their work site, including essential furnishings to ensure a comfortable stay during the internship.401(k) & Company MatchEligibility to participate in the company 401(k) plan with a 10–50% company match that vests immediately.Employee DiscountsAccess to discounts on hotels, vehicles, and other goods and services through Steel Dynamics’ nationwide partner network.Employee Assistance ProgramUp to five free visits per issue, per year for counseling, legal advice, financial guidance, and other daily living resources.Intern ExtravaganzaA two-day event at company headquarters featuring facility tours, networking with company leaders, cultural immersion, and connecting with other interns from across the country.Competitive PayCompetitive hourly wages for all internship positions, rewarding the value interns bring to the company. What Are My Responsibilities as an Electrical Engineering Intern at Steel Dynamics?Assist with substation reliability and preventative maintenance through inspections, documentation, and spare parts planning.Support engineering teams on safety initiatives, including labeling, schematic review, and lockout/tagout procedures.Participate in upgrade and installation projects by reviewing diagrams, updating schematics, and supporting system documentation.Contribute to instrumentation and control projects by assisting with HMI programming, logic development, and monitoring systems.Assist in troubleshooting and repairing electrical systems, including sourcing replacement components and supporting system restoration.Perform inventory management tasks such as cataloging materials, preparing bills of materials, and assisting with procurement planning.Gain hands-on field experience by shadowing electricians during installations, maintenance, and troubleshooting.Collaborate with contractors, vendors, and internal teams on electrical projects and process improvements. What Qualifications Do I Need?Candidates should be enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program in Electrical Engineering or Electrical Engineering Technology.Degree program or experience should include one or more of the following: electrical machinery, power distribution, PLCs/automation systems, power electronics/drives.Preferred GPA of at least 2.7.Examples of Projects Steel Dynamics Electrical Engineering Interns Have CompletedSupport substation reliability by inspecting and documenting current conditions of PTs (Potential Transformers) and CTs (Current Transformers), preparing inventories of available spares, and identifying components that require ordering for contingency planning.Assist with preventative maintenance of high-voltage substations, including reading equipment nameplates, assessing transformer health, and developing documentation based on OEM specifications and site safety standards.Collaborate with engineering teams to optimize safety practices by applying arc flash labels, observing lockout/tagout procedures, and reinforcing “trust but verify” principles when interpreting electrical schematics and prints.Participate in substation upgrade projects by tracing wire diagrams, creating custom wire labels, updating schematics, and loosely managing documentation for labeling systems across GE and TMEIC controls.Contribute to instrumentation and control design by programming HMIs such as C-more for real-time temperature displays and developing logic in Studio 5000 to automate screen changes for furnace monitoring systems.Assist in troubleshooting and rebuilding damaged electrical systems, including camera systems like UNILUX used for surface inspection, and sourcing replacement components for system restoration.Verify and correct electrical blueprints for major furnace systems (e.g., Round-Top-Melter, Tilter-Holder-Furnace), documenting any discrepancies and updating plans to improve installation accuracy and efficiency.Perform standards in live industrial environments.Support cross-functional communication by coordinating with contractors, vendors, and internal departments on projects involving trailer power feeds, jobs.description: Employer: Haworth Expires: 10/10/2026 Tailored Solutions Engineering Intern (onsite) ~ Holland, MICompany OverviewAt Haworth, we're not just creating office furniture; we're shaping dynamic workspaces. As a global leader in workspace solutions, we're on a journey to redefine the future of work. Headquartered in Holland, Michigan, Haworth is a family-owned global powerhouse at the forefront of innovation and sustainable design in the workspace interiors industry. Here, you'll get hands-on with state-of-the-art resources, interact with cross-functional teams of passionate innovators, and experience a blend of global reach and family-owned feel. Whether you're developing new manufacturing processes, implementing smart factory solutions, or designing tomorrow's workspace solutions, you'll be empowered to make a lasting impact.Job OverviewWe are currently looking for a paid Tailored Solutions Engineering Intern to join our team in Holland, MI or possibly Big Rapids, MI. This position will be working onsite at the Haworth Corporate Headquarters. Get ready for an adventurous summer as a Haworth intern! You'll join a cohort of around 50 other dynamic interns for a 12-week program packed with meaningful projects and weekly learning opportunities. You’ll attend NeoCon, the largest commercial design event in the world, where you will get an insider's look at all the latest industry trends and innovations. Sharpen your skills with interactive workshops on networking, public speaking, and using AI tools in a business environment. Connect with mentors and see all areas of the office and manufacturing processes. Then unwind at intern-only social events where you can meet people from all corners of the business. By the end of the summer, you'll leave with real skills, an expanded professional network, and memories to last a lifetime. This is your chance to take your career to new heights! As a Tailored Solutions Engineering Intern, you will have the opportunity to assist with a variety of exciting projects. There are two possibilities for this internship. The first would be an Inquiry Role which is a high volume, fast-paced customer service role with direct interactions with Haworth’s dealers. This department receives 140+ new requests from dealers per day. This role would be to determine if something can be done, the cost, boundary conditions and working with the test lab. CAD Skills may be required. It requires a higher level of engineering to make deviations to a standard project. The intern works in teams of 4-5 people for each specific project. Turnaround is expected the next business day. There is opportunity for the intern to go out and interact with the supplier to determine if the project is feasible. The second Possibility is a Design Role in engineering the design of the project that the dealer has requested, utilizing CAD Skills and working with Bills of material. A single GPU rack can move more than half of its rated load in milliseconds, and when hundreds of racks move together the effect reaches the facility boundary and the grid. We are developing a hybrid energy storage system for data centers to protect upstream infrastructure and increase usable capacity. We are seeking a Research Intern (Hardware Implementation and Validation) to take this system from design to hardware. You will own the implementation and validation of the storage system and its controllers, compare the design's predicted behavior against what the hardware actually does, and feed the differences back into the design. Where the measurements show that the architecture, sizing, or control law needs to change, you will propose and implement the change. This is a hands-on engineering role with a research component. Results are expected to be reported internally and, where appropriate, to feed conference publications and standards discussions. Job ResponsibilitiesBuild, commission, and safely operate a bench-scale hybrid energy storage system (batteries, supercapacitors, bidirectional DC/DC converters, common DC bus) with programmable loads and a real-time control platform.Implement power-split and energy management controllers on real-time hardware and evaluate candidate control strategies head-to-head under repeatable transient test profiles.Design and execute a validation campaign: define test cases from realistic load traces, instrument the bench at the required time resolution, and measure response time, bus voltage deviation, energy split, and state-of-charge behavior.Compare measured results against simulation models, identify where the models are incomplete (converter dynamics, sensing and communication latency, storage non idealities), and update them.Recommend and implement design updates to storage sizing, converter control bandwidth, and the interface between fast local control loops and the supervisory controller.Document hardware, test procedures, and findings so the work can be reproduced and extended.Communicate results via technical reports, presentations, and contributions to publications and patents as appropriate. A Day in the LifeAlign with technical leads on build milestones, test plans, and success metrics.Work in the lab wiring, commissioning, and debugging converters, storage modules, and instrumentation.Deploy a control design from simulation to the real-time target and run it against transient test profiles.Analyze measurement data, compare it with model predictions, and propose the next design or model change.Present progress through demos, written updates, and research discussions. RequirementsCurrently enrolled in a PhD program (preferred) or MS program in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, or a related field.Solid fundamentals in power systems and power electronics: DC/DC converter topologies and control, DC bus dynamics, and protection.Experience with battery and supercapacitor energy storage, including electrical and thermal characteristics, state-of-charge estimation, and safe handling and testing practices.Experience with control of power converters or energy storage systems: classical loop design, droop control, and exposure to model predictive control or other optimization-based methods.Hands-on laboratory experience building, commissioning, and debugging kilowatt scale power hardware, including use of oscilloscopes, power analyzers, and programmable loads or sources.Proficiency in MATLAB/Simulink and Python, and the ability to move a control design from simulation to a real-time target.Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate across disciplines. Preferred QualificationsExperience with real-time platforms such as Typhoon HIL, dSPACE, OPAL-RT, Speedgoat, or equivalent.Experience with hybrid energy storage systems (battery plus supercapacitor) or microgrid energy management.Familiarity with data center power distribution (UPS, PDU, 48 V and high-voltage DC rack buses) and relevant standards such as IEEE 1159, IEEE 1547, or OCP Open Rack specifications.Experience with hardware-in-the-loop validation and model calibration against measured data.Experience with embedded C or converter firmware.Track record of publications, thesis work, or applied prototypes in power electronics, energy storage control, or DC microgrids. Why This RoleOwn a complete build, measure, and redesign loop on a system aimed at one of the fastest-growing power engineering problems in industry.Work in a purpose-built innovation lab with high-resolution power measurement and a full energy storage stack.Collaborate with a research-driven team spanning power hardware, controls, and machine learning, with real deployment pathways. jobs.title: Ph.D. Intern - Silicon Photonics & Optical Communications (2604414) at Marvell Technology
jobs.description: Employer: Marvell Technology Expires: 10/11/2026 About MarvellMarvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. Your Team, Your ImpactThe AI era runs on light. Every rack of XPUs training a frontier model, every hyperscaler connecting data centers across a metro region, every 1.6T optical module pushing data across a fiber at speeds that didn't exist three years ago — all of it depends on silicon photonics and optical DSP technology that Marvell designs. Marvell's optical team is one of the few places in the world where silicon photonics, coherent DSP, PAM4 signal processing, and co-packaged optics integration are all happening under one roof, at production scale, for the world's largest AI infrastructure operators.The work spans every layer of the AI interconnect hierarchy. At the scale-up layer — connecting XPUs within a rack or cluster to behave as a single logical compute unit — the team is developing silicon photonics light engines for Co-Packaged Optics and Near-Packaged Optics platforms that eliminate the reach and power limitations of copper at the shortest distances. At the scale-out layer — connecting clusters of thousands of XPUs across rows and data center floors — the Ara 3nm PAM4 DSP platform drives 1.6T optical transceivers that set the standard for bandwidth density and power-per-bit efficiency across AI fabric networks. And at the scale-across layer — connecting geographically distributed data centers across metro and regional distances — the Orion 800G coherent DSP powers the COLORZ 800, the industry's first 800ZR/ZR+ pluggable coherent transceiver, carrying 800 Gbps up to 1000km over a single wavelength. These are not incremental improvements. They are fundamental rearchitectings of how data moves inside and between the world's most advanced AI infrastructure.Marvell's Ph.D. Intern Program places doctoral candidates directly inside these active design and research efforts. Projects are selected because they sit at the intersection of Marvell's most pressing optical engineering challenges and the photonics, signal processing, and device physics that define doctoral research in this field. The work is the applied dimension of the academic research a Ph.D. candidate is already pursuing — conducted on production silicon, against real system specifications, for hyperscale customers who are counting on it. What you will take away is something no lab or simulation environment can replicate: the experience of seeing your research become working optical silicon, deployed at scale inside the world's most advanced AI infrastructure. What You Can ExpectAs our Ph.D. Silicon Photonics & Optical Communications Intern, every day you will work on problems at the intersection of photonics, high-speed signal processing, and advanced semiconductor integration. Specifically, you can expect to:Design, simulate, and characterize silicon photonics components and subsystems — including modulators, photodetectors, waveguides, and optical engines — for integration into PAM4 and coherent transceiver platformsDevelop and validate DSP algorithms for high-speed optical links, including equalization, FEC, and signal integrity techniques for PAM4 and coherent modulation formatsWork on optical system modeling and link budget analysis for data center interconnect, co-packaged optics, and near-packaged optics applicationsCollaborate with analog IC design, packaging, and systems engineering teams to bring photonic and electronic components together into integrated transceiver solutionsCharacterize and validate designs in the lab — working with high-speed test equipment, optical measurement tools, and silicon bring-up setupsParticipate in a structured design curriculum alongside your Ph.D. intern peers and present your research findings and design results to the engineering team What We're Looking ForTo thrive in this role, you must have hands-on research experience in photonics, optical communications, or high-speed signal processing — not just coursework familiarity. Specifically:Currently enrolled in a Ph.D. program in Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related field, with a research focus in photonics, optical communications, or high-speed signal processingDemonstrate research experience in one or more of the following: silicon photonics device design and simulation, optical transceiver systems, coherent or direct-detect optical communications, or DSP algorithm development for high-speed linksApply strong fundamentals in photonics and electromagnetics — waveguide theory, modulator physics, photodetector design, or optical link analysisUse simulation and modeling tools relevant to your research area (FDTD, MODE, Lumerical, MATLAB, or equivalent) with confidence and independenceCommunicate research findings and design tradeoffs clearly — you will present your work to the engineering team and defend your approach Preferred QualificationsExperience with PAM4 or coherent modulation formats, FEC, or DSP equalization techniques for optical linksFamiliarity with silicon photonics fabrication processes and design-for-manufacturing considerations in advanced CMOS-compatible platformsExposure to co-packaged optics, near-packaged optics, or optical engine integration for high-density interconnectsLab experience with high-speed optical or electrical test and measurement equipmentFamiliarity with analog IC design or mixed-signal circuits as they relate to optical transceiver front-ends (TIAs, laser drivers, modulators) is a strong plus

Your role involves mastering the art of precise measurements, spatial alignment, and layout implementation to ensure the accurate placement of structures and components on the construction site.During your internship, you'll have the opportunity to learn about and contribute to:Blueprint Interpretation: Learn to interpret architectural and engineering blueprints, understanding the spatial relationships and dimensions depicted in the plans. This internship experience will provide you with valuable skills and insights, preparing you for a rewarding career in construction layout engineering.QualificationsCurrently pursuing a degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field.Familiarity with construction layout techniques, instruments, and software.Proficiency in using AutoCAD, Total Station, and other relevant tools.Ability to interpret project plans, blueprints, and specifications for accurate layout implementation.Meticulous attention to detail to ensure precise measurements and alignment.Clear verbal and written communication skills for effective collaboration with project teams.Willingness to troubleshoot layout challenges and find solutions on-site.Collaborative attitude, capable of working closely with other team members, contractors, and stakeholders.Effective time management skills to meet layout deadlines within project schedules.Ability to work on construction sites, often requiring standing, walking, and working outdoors.About Concrete StrategiesConcrete Strategies is the nation’s leading full-service, design-build, turnkey concrete contractor. Training a frontier model across hundreds of thousands of XPUs, routing over 100 terabits of traffic through a single switch fabric at ~400 nanoseconds of latency, processing optical signals at 1.6T across a data center floor — none of it works without the systems architects, DSP engineers, and algorithm designers who define how data moves, how signals are processed, and how compute is organized at every layer of the stack. At Marvell, that work happens across the full AI interconnect hierarchy: scale-up networks connecting XPUs within a rack using PCIe, UAL, and NVLink-compatible switching; scale-out fabrics interconnecting thousands of XPUs across rows and data center floors through the Teralynx Ethernet switch family — purpose-built for AI, now at 102.4 Tbps with ~400ns latency on the T100; and scale-across connectivity linking geographically distributed data centers through coherent DSP and DCI platforms. The architecture decisions made here define what AI infrastructure can do, at what speed, and at what cost.The work spans multiple disciplines and multiple markets. On the switching side, teams are architecting the next generation of Teralynx switch silicon — designing forwarding pipelines, congestion control algorithms, traffic management systems, and telemetry architectures for AI fabrics running Ultra Ethernet Consortium protocols at 800G and 1.6T. On the DSP side, teams are developing signal processing algorithms for high-speed optical and electrical links across PAM4, coherent, and coherent-lite modulation formats — work that spans data center interconnect, carrier networking, and emerging AI fabric applications. And on the systems side, teams are defining the architecture of custom XPU connectivity platforms, co-packaged optics integration, and the end-to-end connectivity stack that hyperscalers depend on to scale their AI infrastructure.Marvell's Ph.D. Intern Program places doctoral candidates directly inside these active architecture and research efforts. Projects are selected because they sit at the intersection of Marvell's most pressing systems-level challenges and the computer architecture, signal processing theory, and networking algorithms that define doctoral research in electrical engineering and computer science. The work is the applied dimension of the academic research a Ph.D. candidate is already pursuing — conducted at production scale, against real system constraints, for hyperscale customers building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure. What you will take away is something no simulation or academic dataset can replicate: the experience of seeing your architectural decisions and algorithms deployed in silicon running inside the world's largest AI data centers. jobs.title: Mechatronics Engineering Intern at Quantum Signal AI
jobs.description: Employer: Quantum Signal AI Expires: 10/13/2026 This is a paid internship. Compensation for this position begins at $26.50 per hour.Role Summary: Quantum Signal AI is looking for a summer 2027 Mechatronics Engineering Intern. The Mechatronics team designs, builds, tests, and supports mechanical and electronic systems in an R&D environment. As an intern, you will contribute to active engineering projects while working alongside multidisciplinary teams. Successful candidates will have a strong interest in mechanical systems, hands-on engineering work, and continuous learning through real-world applications. We value individuals who enjoy learning new skills, exploring diverse technical challenges, and contributing across multiple areas of a project. Join us for a multifaceted, challenging, and rewarding experience! Location: We are located in Saline, Michigan. This position is in-person to encourage a culture of collaboration and mentorship. What You’ll Do: Design various mounts and mechanisms to support electromechanical systems using CAD software. Build, assemble, and integrate prototype and production hardware, including mechanical and electromechanical subsystems. Troubleshoot systems and identify opportunities for improvement to develop practical engineering solutions. Collaborate with mechanical, electrical, software, and research engineers on active project teams. Participate in design reviews and collaborative problem solving with the Mechatronics team. Perform electrical work including soldering, crimping, creating wire harnesses, etc. Document designs, testing activities, and engineering processes to support project execution and future development efforts. What You’ll Bring: Current enrollment as a Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, or related degree program, with sophomore standing or above. Experience using CAD software (Fusion 360, Catia, SolidWorks, etc.). Hands-on experience through coursework, clubs, competitions, research, personal projects, hobbies, or previous work. Motivation to tackle new challenges and receive constructive feedback. Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot and pursue creative approaches and practical solutions. Strong understanding of core mechanical engineering principles and the ability to apply them to practical challenges. Curiosity, adaptability, and commitment to continuous learning. Ability to apply existing technology to new situations. Ability to lift objects of various shapes, sizes, and weights (up to 30 lbs.). Ability to safely walk and stand for extended periods of time, reach (including above your head), bend, climb, push, pull, twist, squat, and kneel as necessary. Bonus Points For: Experience with hand tools, power tools, and fabrication. Experience with reverse engineering, evaluating, and improving existing mechanical or electromechanical systems. Previous internship, co-op, or work experience in a technical environment. Familiarity with electrical concepts, components, and test equipment. Experience collaborating as a member of multidisciplinary teams. Familiarity with mechanical load simulations or similar. Knowledge of 3D printing and related software. You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you are excited about this role and think you can bring value to Quantum Signal AI, we encourage you to apply! What You’ll Get: Frequent collaboration with a diverse set of teams at QSAI A rare level of work variety and hands-on experience A relaxed, fun community and environment in which to solve interesting problems Opportunity to participate in a 401(k) savings plan Ford AZ-Plan vehicle discounts Mentorship-focused learning that emphasizes engineering fundamentals, hands-on problem solving, and understanding the underlying principles behind the systems we build. Other perks to fuel creativity such as an on-site gymnasium, free drinks and snacks, and a variety of optional team activities Candidates for positions with Quantum Signal AI must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. About QSAI: Founded in 1999, Quantum Signal grew up developing intelligent algorithms and AI. As our engineering R&D services expanded, we later sharpened our focus on applications and technology related to mobility, sensing, perception, autonomy, and simulation. In 2019 we became Quantum Signal AI, a subsidiary of Ford Motor developing technologies to advance their R&D efforts. We build solutions to enhance the capability, robustness, safety, and acceptance of intelligent ground vehicles in an effort to make transportation more effective and efficient for all. While AI is part of our name, our internship program emphasizes building fundamental engineering knowledge, analytical thinking, and practical problem-solving skills. We want interns to understand how and why systems work through hands-on experience, mentorship, and experimentation, rather than simply relying on tools to provide answers. Our HQ in the historic Union School in Saline, MI is the perfect playground to develop this cutting-edge technology and we’re always looking for smart folks who like new challenges, learning new skills, and technical variety.

jobs.description: Employer: Artagon Expires: 10/13/2026 Artagon est une association d’intérêt général dédiée au soutien, à la promotion et à l’accompagnement de la création et des cultures émergentes, en prise avec les enjeux sociétaux actuels.Elle propose toute l’année une pluralité de programmes – création et gestion de lieux ressource, formations, bourses, événements – destinés aux étudiant·es en art, aux artistes et aux professionnel·les de la culture en début de parcours.Artagon est aujourd’hui à la tête de deux lieux ressource dédiés à l’accompagnement de la création émergente en France, avec un fort ancrage local : Artagon Marseille et Artagon Pantin en région parisienne.Avec plus de 7 000 m² d’espaces de travail, de formation et de production, qui rassemblent une centaine de résidents en simultané, Artagon pilote ainsi la première pépinière culturelle pluridisciplinaire et multirégionale en France.Fondée en 2014 par le duo de directeurs artistiques et de commissaires d’exposition Anna Labouze & Keimis Henni, ses actions sont portées par une équipe d’une dizaine de personnes.Afin de soutenir le développement de ses activités dans le champ de la formation professionnelle, l’association Artagon propose un stage au sein de son organisme de formation certifié Qualiopi, créé en 2025.Artagon accompagne les artistes et porteur·euses de projets culturels dans le développement de leurs compétences et la structuration de leurs parcours professionnels. Les formations proposées sont conçues au plus près des réalités du secteur.Au sein de l’écosystème culturel, le stage offre une immersion concrète dans le fonctionnement d’un organisme de formation. Le poste s’inscrit dans une logique de suivi des personnes intéressées pour s’inscrire à une formation, avec un accompagnement attentif pour faciliter leur accès aux formations et les aider dans leurs démarches de financement. L’objectif est de garantir un accompagnement personnalisé, depuis la prise de contact jusqu’à l’accès effectif aux formations.Le/la stagiaire travaillera en lien direct avec la responsable de l’organisme de formation et participera activement à l’expérience des personnes souhaitant intégrer une formation, de leur premier contact jusqu’à l’issue de la formation.Ce que vous allez apprendreComprendre le fonctionnement d’un organisme de formation certifié (Qualiopi)Développer des compétences en relation client dans un contexte B2CDécouvrir les mécanismes de financement de la formation professionnelleParticiper au développement et à la diffusion d’offres de formationUtiliser des outils de suivi (CRM, devis, facturation)Gagner en réflexe et en autonomie dans la gestion de projetsMissions principales1. Suivi de relation clientAssurer le suivi des personnes intéressées tout au long de leur parcours d’inscription.Répondre aux demandes d’informations, assurer un premier niveau de relation commerciale et orienter selon les besoins.Contribuer à la qualité de l’expérience et à la satisfaction.2. Appui à la gestion administrative et suivi commercialContribuer au suivi administratif des dossiers.Assurer le suivi des devis (édition, envoi, relance).Effectuer les relances commerciales (devis, factures, paiements).Mettre à jour les outils de suivi et bases de données.3. Participation à l’organisation des formationsContribuer à la préparation logistique des sessions.Être un point de contact pour les stagiaires tout au long de la formation.Suivre les retours (questionnaires, bilans).Archiver les documents administratifs.4. Veille et diffusion des offresRéaliser une veille sur les plateformes, annuaires et sites spécialisés dans la formation.Identifier les opportunités de diffusion des offres de formation.Mettre à jour et publier les formations sur les plateformes et annuaires pertinents.Garantir la bonne visibilité des offres sur les supports de diffusion externes.Profil recherchéFormation en commerce, marketing ou équivalentIntérêt pour le développement d’activité et la relation avec les publicsBonne aisance relationnelle et rédactionnelleOrganisation, rigueur et sens des prioritésIntérêt pour la vente et le développement commercialEsprit d’initiative, réactivité et autonomieMaîtrise des outils bureautiquesSensibilité pour le milieu culturel et appétence pour le secteur de la formation

Understanding of experimental design principles in corrosion science and engineering.Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical skills.Demonstrated ability and desire to learn in a research-focused environment.Employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.This position requires access to controlled technology, as defined in the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. §730, et seq.) and/or the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Authorizations from the relevant government agency may be required to meet export control compliance requirements.Preferred Qualifications:Enrolled in a Ph.D. program.Experience working in a laboratory environment with corrosion testing equipment.Experience analyzing and interpreting metallographic data and test results.Interest in corrosion science, materials development, and manufacturing applications.

jobs.title: Aviation Analyst Intern at Cignus Consulting
jobs.description: Employer: Cignus Consulting Expires: 10/14/2026 About CignusCignus Consulting is an SBA 8(a)-certified, MBE/DBE aviation technology and engineering firm headquartered in Leesburg, Virginia. Since 2007 we have supported the FAA, NASA, DoD, airport authorities, and aviation clients with systems engineering, airspace and airside simulation, aviation data analytics, and software products built on standards like SWIM, ADS-B, and ARINC 424. Our work ranges from federal task orders and SBIR research to commercial simulation and digital twin platforms.We are a small team doing technically serious work, which means the person in this role will do real research, not observe it.The RoleWe are looking for an Aviation Analyst Intern to support our research in runway and surface safety. One effort extends runway incursion and approach risk monitoring across major airports. The other brings surface surveillance to the many U.S. towered airports that cannot justify the cost of ASDE-X.This role supplies the operational aviation judgment the research depends on. Our engineers build the models, but deciding whether a controller's instruction was actually complied with takes someone who understands how the operation works.What You Will DoReview archived ground and tower audio, correct model transcriptions, and annotate what was said (callsigns, taxi routes, runway assignments, hold-short instructions, crossing authorizations) to build the evaluation sets our speech models are measured againstAnnotate aircraft and vehicle movements in recorded surveillance and camera data, identifying what each target was doing and where the evidence becomes ambiguousCompile a register of runway incursions and anomalous events from ASRS, NTSB, ASIAS, and FAA Runway Safety sources, and assess which ones can be reconstructed from our archivesProduce the ground-truth datasets used to measure detection rate, false alert rate, and alert lead timeCoordinate quarterly reviews with our expert panel of controllers, pilots, and airport operations staff, including scheduling, pre-read materials, and recordsRequired QualificationsCurrent student or recent graduate in aviation management, aerospace engineering, professional flight, air traffic management, or a related disciplineAviation background through flight training, ATC coursework or training, or work experience at an airport, airline, FBO, or flight schoolEnough operational familiarity to follow a ground control frequency and anticipate what should happen next. A pilot certificate or ATC coursework is the strongest indicator we look forConsistency and attention to detail across long annotation tasks. Labeling is the foundation the research rests on, and inconsistency propagates silently into every downstream resultWorking comfort with Python notebooks, or the ability to get there quickly. Substantial programming experience is not requiredU.S. work authorizationPreferred QualificationsPrivate pilot certificate or higher, or completion of an FAA AT-CTI or comparable ATC programFamiliarity with ASDE-X, ADS-B, NOTAM, ATIS, or METAR dataExperience with video or audio annotation toolsPrior exposure to FAA or NASA datasetsInterest in a career in aviation safety, air traffic management, or aviation technologyWork StructureRemote or hybrid. Remote candidates are welcome, and candidates in the DC region are invited to work from our Leesburg office. You will need to be available for regular working sessions during U.S. Eastern business hours. Compensation$20 to $30 per hour, depending on academic level and aviation experience. To ApplySend a resume and a short note on one aviation experience (a flight lesson, a tower visit, a class project, an airport job) where you had to figure out what was really happening in the operation, and how you figured it out.

jobs.description: Employer: Church & Dwight Co., Inc. Expires: 10/15/2026 General Summary:In this role, you will assist in providing technical support to improve the reliability of our packaging operations through learning how to follow and implement continuous improvement methodologies. The successful candidate will have a strong focus on safety, excellent communication skills, and the ability to prioritize work assignments in a fast-paced environment. Essential Functions:Promote a safety culture and awareness within the area of responsibility.Assist with design and modify new products and equipment, as well as supporting existing designs.Helps identify processing and packaging improvement opportunities using Lean manufacturing techniques.Leverages process data and other digital solutions to track operational key performance indicators (KPI) such as production throughput, unplanned downtime, and scrap. Generates reports, trends and Paretos to drive targeted actions and countermeasures to the plant abnormalities. Work with the Training department to build and develop effective training systems and organize training sessions as needed. SME for Training Within Industry (TWI).Creates, manages, and executes the CI systems and processes that improve OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) through the Church and Dwight Lean pillars of 5S & Visual management, Lean Daily Management, and Kaizen ProjectsUtilize root cause analysis techniques to solve issues in a permanent and sustainable manner.Help identify potential issues and mitigate risks using failure mode and effects analysis.Collaborate with cross-functional teams to address technical challenges and achieve objectives.Help create and update standard work to promote training and sustainment.Ensure fair and consistent adherence to local and corporate policies and procedures.Perform other related duties as required and assigned. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:Ability to communicate clearly and concisely in multiple media forms – verbal, written, etc.Organizational and time management skills.Ability to prioritize work assignments in a fast-paced work environment.Knowledge of production operation, including equipment, materials, workflow, etc.Ability to always maintain absolute confidentiality and in all situations. Education:Currently pursuing a degree in Engineering or a related fieldFamiliar with using RCA, fishbone, 5-why, quick kaizen, and FMEA methodologies.Computer skills, including in MS Office Suite, MS Power BIStrong desire to learn and grow in all areas, as well as the willingness to share knowledge with others. Church & Dwight Co., Inc. is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities
